# Contributing to Keyline

## Set up

Node.js 24 (`.nvmrc`), then:

```sh
npm ci
npx playwright install chrome webkit     # the browser tests use Chrome and Playwright's WebKit; on Linux add --with-deps
```

## How the repository fits together

Keyline ships as a shadcn **registry**: a set of **items** (a component, a shared library, the theme) that the
shadcn CLI copies into someone else's project. Everything else in the repository exists to build, exercise or
document those items.

- **`src/registry/`** is the product. `src/registry/keyline/` holds the source (each component is
  `ui/<name>.tsx` with its `ui/<name>.css`), and `src/registry/manifest.mjs` lists the items and the files each
  one ships.
- **`site/public/r/`** is the built registry, one JSON file per item, which is what `npx shadcn add` downloads.
  The documentation site serves it at `/r/{name}.json`, so deploying the site publishes the registry. It is
  generated by `npm run registry:build` and committed. The build reads imports and `kl-` class names to work out
  each item's npm and registry dependencies, so the manifest names files only, and it fails when a file that
  needs `"use client";` lacks it (written with the semicolon; the build script says why).
- **`src/lib/utils.ts` and `components.json`** stand in for a consumer's shadcn setup. Components import `cn()`
  from `@/lib/utils`, as they will in an installed project (`@/` is `src/`).
- **`src/demo/`** is the demo app (`npm run dev`). Its specimen page shows every component in its states, one
  **specimen** per component in `src/demo/specimens/`. The browser tests run against it.
- **`site/`** is the documentation site (`npm run site:dev`): a page and examples per component, built with
  Keyline's own components.
- **`tests/`** holds unit tests (`tests/*.test.ts`), browser specs (`tests/browser/`, see its
  [README](../tests/browser/README.md)) and consumer checks (`tests/consumer/`), which install items into fresh
  projects.
- **`docs/`** holds [usage.md](../docs/usage.md) for people installing Keyline, [design.md](../docs/design.md) for
  the design model every component follows, and [releasing.md](../docs/releasing.md) for publishing a version.

## Making a change

1. Edit the component in `src/registry/keyline/` and watch its specimen in `npm run dev`.
2. Run the specs for what you touched: `npx playwright test <name>` runs every spec whose file name matches, in
   both engines. Each run builds its own snapshot of the app, so edits made while it runs are not tested.
3. Look at it across modes when the change is visible. `npm run capture -- <data-testid>` screenshots one element
   in light, dark, compact, RTL, narrow and reduced-motion configurations in both engines, and writes the images to
   `.artifacts/captures/`. The specs assert on geometry, styles and the accessibility tree rather than pixels, so
   this is how a visual change gets seen.
4. If the change affects what an item installs (its files, CSS, imports, or the manifest), run
   `npm run registry:build` and commit `site/public/r/` with it. CI fails when it is out of date.
5. Run `npm run check` before opening a pull request. It covers types, unit tests (including the install commands
   in the docs and the built registry), the `.editorconfig` format check, the registry build, every browser spec
   and the CSS-order check, and takes about five minutes.

Two slower checks run when they apply:

- `npm run test:consumer`, when a change affects installation. It installs items from a fresh registry build into
  new Vite + shadcn apps (all together, one at a time, and with the opt-in shadcn theme) and a Next.js App Router
  app (`src/`, a `~/*` alias, stock shadcn beside Keyline, repeated installs), then type-checks, builds and
  exercises them in Chrome and WebKit. It needs network access. CI runs it on every pull request.
- `npm run test:site`, when a change affects the documentation site. Start the site first with
  `npm run site:build && npm run site:start`.

All test, capture and consumer output goes to `.artifacts/`, which is ignored.

## Adding a component

A new component is done when it has all of these:

- source in `src/registry/keyline/ui/`, following [docs/design.md](../docs/design.md)
- an entry in `src/registry/manifest.mjs`, with `site/public/r/` rebuilt
- a specimen in `src/demo/specimens/`, wired into `src/demo/App.tsx`
- a page and example in `site/`
- browser specs in `tests/browser/` covering behaviour, keyboard, focus and the accessibility tree in both engines

## Rules, and why

- **Demos, the site and consumer tests use the public API.** Compose with props, Tailwind utilities and the `kl-`
  role utilities, and hook tests onto `data-testid`. Internal `.kl-*` classes can change at any time, and a
  consumer has nothing else to work with. When a composition seems to need an internal class, that is an API gap:
  fix the component, or record the gap.
- **Wrap the library shadcn uses** for the same job (react-resizable-panels, react-day-picker, recharts,
  embla-carousel), pinned to an exact version, and build everything else on Base UI primitives. Hand-written
  behaviour misses the edge cases those libraries already handle.
- **The documentation site is built from Keyline**: its shell, navigation, scroll areas and tables are Keyline
  components. That way the site keeps testing the library.
- **Fix the cause.** A failure that depends on sub-pixel position or timing gets its bias removed, the fix is
  checked across offsets, and the guard test is shown to fail on the old code.
- **A check stays as strict as it was.** Fix the code rather than loosen an assertion or a tolerance. A
  `test.skip` names the engine limitation that requires it.

## Pull requests

Keep each pull request to one change, and say what a reviewer should look at. Visible changes need before and
after captures.
